entity:meth_00107.name: Comprehensive review of AI-driven multiscale modeling approaches for solid‑state physics and chemistry

selected.text: Current challenges limiting AI‑driven multiscale modeling include limited data availability, restricted model transferability, and limited explainability.
Graph neural network architectures such as MEGNet and SchNet enhance prediction of phase transitions, defect dynamics, and bulk material properties relative to classical computational approaches.

Integrating renormalization‑group concepts with machine‑learning architectures has been used to predict transitions to canted antiferromagnetic phases in 3D Ising and Fermi‑Hubbard models, to classify quantum phases, and to recognize complex many‑body phases from raw simulation data.
Future integration of formal renormalization‑group concepts with machine‑learning architectures is a promising direction for modeling systems near criticality or with strong electron correlations.

entity:arti_00013.name: A SURVEY OF AI FOR MATERIALS SCIENCE: FOUNDATION MODELS, LLM AGENTS, DATASETS, AND TOOLS

selected.text: Foundation models enable cross-domain generalization and emergent capabilities for scientific discovery in materials science.

MatterSim, a zero‑shot machine‑learned interatomic potential trained on >17 million DFT‑labeled structures, supports universal simulation across all elements, temperatures and pressures, achieving energy prediction errors below 50 meV/atom even in high‑temperature, non‑equilibrium regimes.

Current foundation models in materials science suffer from limited generalizability, interpretability, data imbalance, safety concerns, inability to model long‑range interactions (electrostatics, dispersion, magnetism), and lack of synthesizability, phase‑stability, or safety constraints, restricting experimental feasibility of generated candidates.

The survey proposes a task‑driven taxonomy that organizes foundation models into six application areas: data extraction/interpretation/Q&A, atomistic simulation, property prediction, materials structure/design/discovery, process planning/discovery/optimization, and multiscale modeling.

entity:meth_00140.name: Uncertainty-aware graph convolutional neural network for vibrational free‑energy prediction

selected.text: The presented workflow enables high‑throughput prediction of temperature‑induced solid‑solid phase transitions without performing explicit phonon calculations for each material, dramatically reducing computational cost.

Screening of approximately 50 000 inorganic crystals with the machine‑learning model identified over 2 000 temperature‑induced solid‑solid polymorphic transitions between 300 K and 600 K, including 130 stable transitions within the technologically relevant 300 K–350 K interval.

Several predicted solid‑solid transitions show large entropy changes exceeding 300 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹ (e.g., Li₃MnF₇: 342.3 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹, PnCl₂: 338.3 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹, Fe₄OF₇: 252.1 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹), while the highest entropy changes (> 400 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹) are limited to transitions above 450 K and occur exclusively in nonpolar‑nonpolar categories, reducing their relevance for room‑temperature applications.

Validation against experimental reports and independent first‑principles calculations confirms the robustness and predictive power of the ML‑guided framework, with reasonable agreement for transition temperatures of KNO₃, KNO₂ and CaCO₃, DFT‑calculated free‑energy differences matching ML predictions for a ten‑material subset, and thermal‑conductivity ratios for Li₄TiS₄ and NaNO₃ closely reproduced by DFT.

selected.text: GNoME-driven molecular dynamics simulations on 623 materials with previously unseen compositions enable classification of unseen compositions as superionic conductors in comparison with AIMD.

Crystal structures, data, and software for analyzing stable crystals, phase diagrams, static GNN, and interatomic potentials will be made available at the Google DeepMind materials_discovery GitHub repository and via the Materials Project with permanent DOI link 10.17188/2009989.

GNNs trained on large and diverse first-principles calculations increase the number of stable crystals by more than an order of magnitude, with scaling showing consistent power-law improvements in MLIP accuracy and generalization on out-of-distribution structural tasks.

More than 10⁹ candidate structures were generated over the course of active learning using symmetry-aware partial substitutions and random structure search, with 232,477 out of 381,000 stable structures (approximately 61%) attributed to the SAPS candidate generation procedure.
GNoME discovered over 2.2 million new stable inorganic materials and more than 45 000 new crystal prototypes, an order‑of‑magnitude increase over prior discovery efforts.
GNoME was trained on an in-house database of roughly 80 million DFT calculations.

entity:meth_00437.name: two-step supervised-unsupervised melting temperature prediction with symbolic regression

selected.text: A curated dataset of 476 binary ionic compound melting temperatures spanning 0-4,000°C was compiled for machine learning model development.

The two-step clustering approach provides interpretability by revealing different melting physics dominated by bonding types, with Cluster 1 governed by ionic bonding features and Cluster 2 by covalent bonding features.
Cohesive energy and elastic moduli (shear and bulk modulus) are the most important features for melting temperature prediction, as identified by both ensemble feature importance and SHAP analysis.

Cluster 2 melting temperatures can be accurately represented with symbolic models depending on only two features: squared cohesive energy and inverse square root of periodic groups or electronegativities.

entity:meth_00232.name: Graph Neural Network for atomic property prediction in defective crystalline solids

selected.text: Including tensile strain as an input node feature enables the GNN to accurately predict stress evolution during loading, reproducing nonlinear strain‑stress curves for porous graphene.

The GNN framework generalizes across defect types (grain boundaries, vacancies) and material dimensionalities (2D graphene, 3D aluminum), and to unseen defect configurations in over 10⁶ porous graphene structures, maintaining high prediction accuracy despite being trained on only about 1,200 random samples.
The GNN predicts atomic tensile stress in porous graphene membranes under tensile strain with a mean normalized relative error of 4.9% and a maximum error of about 10%.

Coupling the GNN with a genetic algorithm efficiently discovers optimal holey graphene designs (e.g., arrow‑shaped hole patterns) that achieve significantly lower stress concentration than suboptimal designs, using only ~800 stress evaluations—an order of magnitude fewer than brute‑force search—and reliably locates the global minimum in most of 1,000 random initializations.

selected.text: Machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on OMat24 predict tightly converged DFT forces with accuracy comparable to or better than predictions for less tightly converged calculations.

OMat24 comprises over 118 million DFT calculations across diverse chemistries, materials, and configurations for inorganic bulk materials, making it up to 2 orders of magnitude larger than other openly available datasets in terms of number of single-point calculations.

MLIP models trained on OMat24 achieve F1 scores above 0.9 for stability prediction and 20 meV/atom accuracy for formation energy on Matbench Discovery, with all five top-performing models on the Matbench Discovery leaderboard exclusively trained on OMat24.

The mean absolute error between DFT predicted and experimental formation energies for 222 compounds is 55 meV/atom using OMat24 DFT settings, with compatibility corrections computed following the Materials Project MP2020 Compatibility scheme.

Training a TensorNet model on the 400 k‑structure MatPES‑PBE dataset requires approximately 15 minutes per epoch on a single RTX A6000 GPU, whereas training on the 100 M‑structure OMat24 dataset needs about 20 hours per epoch on sixteen A100 GPUs, highlighting the computational efficiency of MatPES.
Rattled systems in the OMat24 dataset have deleterious effects on model performance when evaluated on out-of-distribution hetero-diatomic systems.

entity:arti_00047.name: Challenges and opportunities for machine learning in multiscale computational modeling

selected.text: Concurrent multiscale modeling approaches face formidable computation costs as the problem size increases.

ML-based simulation can achieve comparable fidelity to direct numerical simulation while being considerably faster in computation time, with convolutional neural networks producing high-fidelity estimation of materials microstructure response with multiple orders of magnitude faster computation.
Hierarchical multiscale modeling approaches require large amounts of memory and storage space to store precomputed quantities of interest.
Machine learning can serve as a surrogate for, accelerate, or augment traditional numerical methods in multiscale computational modeling.

entity:meth_00383.name: DeePMD training protocol for diffusion coefficient computation

selected.text: The proposed training protocol based on augmenting the training set via intermediate molecular dynamics simulations can assess the quality of approximate trajectories and computed physical properties.

The DeePMD model successfully reproduces the superionic behavior of solid-state electrolytes with linear Lithium/Sodium mean squared displacement over time and diffusion coefficient uncertainty of about 20% or smaller, which is precise enough for battery applications.
For LLZO, the computed activation energies range from 0.2 to 0.22 eV, in very good agreement with experimental values of 0.20-0.21 eV for cubic LLZO.
Starting the training loop with sufficient data sampling a relevant portion of phase space is important for obtaining generalizable models.

entity:arti_00023.name: Linking atomic structural defects to mesoscale properties in crystalline solids using graph neural networks

selected.text: Including tensile strain as an input node feature enables the GNN to accurately predict stress evolution during loading, reproducing nonlinear strain‑stress curves for porous graphene.

The GNN framework generalizes across defect types (grain boundaries, vacancies) and material dimensionalities (2D graphene, 3D aluminum), and to unseen defect configurations in over 10⁶ porous graphene structures, maintaining high prediction accuracy despite being trained on only about 1,200 random samples.
The GNN predicts atomic tensile stress in porous graphene membranes under tensile strain with a mean normalized relative error of 4.9% and a maximum error of about 10%.

Coupling the GNN with a genetic algorithm efficiently discovers optimal holey graphene designs (e.g., arrow‑shaped hole patterns) that achieve significantly lower stress concentration than suboptimal designs, using only ~800 stress evaluations—an order of magnitude fewer than brute‑force search—and reliably locates the global minimum in most of 1,000 random initializations.

entity:meth_00134.name: Frozen-framework potential energy surface (PES) descriptor screening

selected.text: The SevenNet machine-learned interatomic potential outperforms the earlier M3GNet model on the Matbench Discovery benchmark.

Using an ML‑trained interatomic potential (ML‑IAP) enables validation of many more candidate structures than conventional AIMD, as demonstrated by MD simulations on 30 random and 100 top‑Ξ structures.

Computing the frozen‑framework PES descriptors for 5997 Materials Project structures required seven days on a 48‑core CPU with two RTX 6000 GPUs, comparable to the time needed for ML‑driven MD on 100 materials.

Using the frozen‑framework approximation, where only a single Li ion moves while the host lattice remains fixed, reduces the generalization error of the ML‑IAP compared with fully relaxed MD or NEB simulations.

entity:arti_00051.name: Discovering Melting Temperature Prediction Models of Inorganic Solids by Combining Supervised and Unsupervised Learning

selected.text: A curated dataset of 476 binary ionic compound melting temperatures spanning 0-4,000°C was compiled for machine learning model development.

The two-step clustering approach provides interpretability by revealing different melting physics dominated by bonding types, with Cluster 1 governed by ionic bonding features and Cluster 2 by covalent bonding features.
Cohesive energy and elastic moduli (shear and bulk modulus) are the most important features for melting temperature prediction, as identified by both ensemble feature importance and SHAP analysis.

Cluster 2 melting temperatures can be accurately represented with symbolic models depending on only two features: squared cohesive energy and inverse square root of periodic groups or electronegativities.

entity:meth_00407.name: long-range MLIP generalization framework with biased train-test splitting

selected.text: Long-range correction schemes in machine learning interatomic potentials are essential for achieving state-of-the-art accuracy, improving in-distribution performance, and enabling significant gains in transferability to unseen regions of chemical space.

Metal-organic frameworks present an ideal application for MLIPs because classical force fields lack required accuracy while DFT is too computationally expensive for large unit cells and long timescales.

Biased train-test splitting strategies including cluster, maximal separation, size, and random splits enable rigorous benchmarking by explicitly testing model performance in significantly different regions of chemical space.

Latent Ewald Summation cannot infer correct partial charges without reference charge labels and frequently predicts charges near zero or opposite in sign to reference values in challenging chemical environments such as MOFs.

selected.text: The AFLOW standard enables reproducible high-throughput DFT calculations through standardized parameter sets for k-point density, energy cut-offs, exchange-correlation functionals, pseudopotentials, DFT+U parameters, and convergence criteria.
The PBE functional combined with PAW potentials is the default exchange-correlation functional and potential combination for ICSD, Binary Alloy, and Heusler databases.

Specific Ueff parameters are defined for d-block elements (Table 4) and U, J parameters for f-block elements (Table 5) to correct self-interaction error in DFT+U calculations, with values ranging from 1.9 eV (In) to 7.5 eV (Zn).

Electronic convergence criteria are δEelec = 10⁻⁵ eV and ionic convergence criteria are δEion = 10⁻⁴ eV for Elements database entries, while all other databases use δEelec = 10⁻³ eV and δEion = 10⁻² eV.

selected.text: The presented scale‑bridging framework, linking DFT‑informed statistical mechanics to continuum phase‑field models via IDNN‑learned free‑energy functions, constitutes the first systematic implementation of this kind for LiCoO₂ cathodes.

Representing molecular dynamics results as image‑based geometric matrices preserves crystal orientation information and allows the neural network to learn spatiotemporal fracture behavior.

A model trained exclusively on single‑crystal data generalizes to bicrystal and gradient‑orientation crystals, reproducing MD fracture patterns for small orientation differences, capturing overall crack paths for large orientation differences, and handling arbitrary geometry gradients.
The ConvLSTM approach reduces computational cost dramatically compared with full molecular dynamics simulations, enabling rapid fracture predictions.

entity:arti_00010.name: Bridging scales with Machine Learning: From first principles statistical mechanics to continuum phase field computations to study order-disorder transitions in LixCoO2

selected.text: The presented scale‑bridging framework, linking DFT‑informed statistical mechanics to continuum phase‑field models via IDNN‑learned free‑energy functions, constitutes the first systematic implementation of this kind for LiCoO₂ cathodes.

Phase‑field simulations reproduce the lever‑rule mass fractions of ordered and disordered phases predicted by the Monte Carlo phase diagram after accounting for a slight shift in the order‑disorder boundaries from the IDNN free‑energy surface.

Integrable Deep Neural Networks trained on derivative (chemical‑potential) data accurately learn the high‑dimensional free‑energy density and chemical‑potential functions for LiₓCoO₂, achieving mean‑squared errors comparable to the reported minima and reproducing DFT formation energies with a mean absolute error below 5 meV atom⁻¹.
Semi‑Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations predict an order‑disorder transition temperature slightly above 330 K for the x≈0.5 zig‑zag ordering, in agreement with experimental observations.

selected.text: Machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on OMat24 predict tightly converged DFT forces with accuracy comparable to or better than predictions for less tightly converged calculations.

OMat24 comprises over 118 million DFT calculations across diverse chemistries, materials, and configurations for inorganic bulk materials, making it up to 2 orders of magnitude larger than other openly available datasets in terms of number of single-point calculations.

MLIP models trained on OMat24 achieve F1 scores above 0.9 for stability prediction and 20 meV/atom accuracy for formation energy on Matbench Discovery, with all five top-performing models on the Matbench Discovery leaderboard exclusively trained on OMat24.

The mean absolute error between DFT predicted and experimental formation energies for 222 compounds is 55 meV/atom using OMat24 DFT settings, with compatibility corrections computed following the Materials Project MP2020 Compatibility scheme.

entity:arti_00032.name: Commentary: The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation

selected.text: High‑throughput computational screening through the Materials Project has screened tens of thousands of compounds and identified promising candidates for solar water splitting, photovoltaics, topological insulators, scintillators, CO₂ capture, piezoelectrics, thermoelectrics, catalysis, hydrogen storage, and Li‑ion batteries, with experimental hits reported in several areas.
Class‑specific computational methodologies and reference reactions are applied for solid‑gas, d‑block oxide, and dissolved‑ion systems to improve agreement with experimental data.

The distribution of chromium coordination environments in oxides derived from the database matches known chemical principles: Cr⁶⁺ prefers tetrahedral (4‑fold) coordination, while Cr³⁺ prefers octahedral (6‑fold) coordination.

EquiformerV2 can scale Lmax to 6 or 8 on OC20 dataset using eSCN convolutions that reduce computational cost from O(L^6) to O(L^3), whereas original Equiformer is impractical for Lmax > 2 on large-scale datasets.

EquiformerV2+DeNS (a universal interatomic potential) achieves the highest classification performance among all evaluated models, with F1 scores up to 0.983, ROC AUC 0.96, and discovery acceleration factors up to 6.33, establishing state‑of‑the‑art for ML‑guided materials discovery.
UMA-M reduces OC20 S2EF adsorption energy prediction errors by approximately 80% compared to previous state-of-the-art models, achieving 33.4 meV MAE versus 149.1 meV for EquiformerV2-OC20.

Extrapolation performance degrades with increasing WBM batch number for most models, especially Wrenformer and Voronoi RF, while universal interatomic potential models (e.g., EquiformerV2, ORB) show minimal degradation across batches.

selected.text: The proposed training protocol based on augmenting the training set via intermediate molecular dynamics simulations can assess the quality of approximate trajectories and computed physical properties.

The DeePMD model successfully reproduces the superionic behavior of solid-state electrolytes with linear Lithium/Sodium mean squared displacement over time and diffusion coefficient uncertainty of about 20% or smaller, which is precise enough for battery applications.
For LLZO, the computed activation energies range from 0.2 to 0.22 eV, in very good agreement with experimental values of 0.20-0.21 eV for cubic LLZO.
Starting the training loop with sufficient data sampling a relevant portion of phase space is important for obtaining generalizable models.

A Hubbard U parameter of 2.5 eV in DFT+U (with a vdW‑DF exchange‑correlation functional) reproduces the experimental average lithiation voltages of LiCoO₂ across the composition ranges {0‑1}, {0‑0.5}, and {0.5‑1}.
The AFLOW Standard for High-Throughput Materials Science Calculations

selected.text: Combined two-body, three-body, and SOAP many-body descriptors are necessary for GAP to achieve the accuracy limit imposed by force locality and make physically meaningful predictions; models using only subsets of descriptors produce unphysical structures during molecular dynamics simulations.
GAP radial and angular distribution functions for liquid and amorphous carbon closely match DFT reference results, including peak locations, extents, and overall curve shapes.

The training database includes liquid and amorphous structures, randomly distorted crystalline allotropes (diamond and graphite), and isolated dimer DFT data, extended iteratively by performing melt-quench simulations driven by previous GAP versions with DFT single-point computations for validation snapshots.

GAP sp3 concentration predictions are closer to DFT reference than empirical Brenner and Tersoff potentials, particularly at lower densities; empirical potentials underestimate sp3 concentration in tetrahedral amorphous carbon.

selected.text: DeePMD-kit supports interpolation between Deep Potential models and empirical pairwise potentials for cases where DFT calculations fail at close interatomic distances.
DeePMD-kit is an open-source software package that facilitates molecular dynamics simulations using Deep Potential machine learning potentials for computational chemistry and materials science.
DeePMD-kit can simulate systems containing almost all periodic table elements including drug-like molecules, ions, transition states, and excited states.
The fitting network can fit potential energy, force, virial, and tensorial properties such as dipole and polarizability.
